title: How Pinterest Secures AWS Infrastructure at Scale with a Centralized Terraform Pipeline
gist: Pinterest disclosed its private Resource Provisioner Pipeline (RPP), a centralized GitHub Actions Terraform engine that uses OIDC role chaining, workspace-to-role mapping and dual human control to enforce least privilege across a still-fragmented multi-repo AWS estate. Its distinguishing control is validating that a workspace's Terraform code path matches its declared S3 backend and KMS key before any role is assumed, guarding against cross-workspace state corruption — a pattern contrasted with Mercari's per-service GCP impersonation and Slack's decentralized state ownership.

insights.claim: Pinterest has built and disclosed an internal Terraform execution engine called the Resource Provisioner Pipeline (RPP) that governs AWS changes across many Terraform workspaces controlling thousands of cloud resources including IAM policies, VPCs, load balancers, S3 buckets and Kubernetes clusters.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Large consumer platforms are internalising IaC governance rather than buying it, a headwind for commercial Terraform-governance vendors selling into big-tech accounts.
insights.quote: Pinterest has revealed the Resource Provisioner Pipeline (RPP), its own Terraform execution engine.

insights.claim: RPP runs as a central set of composite GitHub Actions triggered on pull request events rather than per-repo scripts, and splits a single PR into separate plan/apply runs for each affected Terraform workspace.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Confirms GitHub Actions is being used as the control plane for regulated infrastructure change at scale, deepening GitHub's lock-in inside enterprise CI/CD.
insights.quote: It runs as a central set of composite GitHub Actions instead of per-repo scripts.
insights.locator: RPP activates on GitHub pull request events

insights.claim: Privilege is granted through a chained-role model: a workflow first assumes a central RPPActionsRole restricted to pre-authorised GitHub workflows via OIDC token validation, then reads a source-of-truth config mapping each workspace to its allowed repository, working directory, owning team and execution IAM role before assuming the down-scoped team role.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Keyless OIDC role chaining is now the de facto standard for CI-to-cloud auth; static cloud credentials in CI are becoming a legacy audit finding.
insights.quote: This role is limited to certain pre-authorised GitHub workflows through OIDC token validation.

insights.claim: The pipeline runs `terraform fmt` and `plan` automatically but only executes `apply` after an explicit human comment on the pull request, keeping plan and apply as separate auditable actions.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Plan-then-apply gating with an explicit human trigger is the emerging control auditors will expect in IaC pipelines; tooling that cannot express it is at a disadvantage.
insights.quote: Dual control has two layers: a human code review approval and a clear PR comment needed to trigger the apply.

insights.claim: Before down-scoping to a team role, RPP validates that the Terraform code path matches the specific S3 backend and KMS key declared for that workspace, catching cases where a developer accidentally points one workspace's directory at another's state file.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Cross-workspace state corruption is an under-priced operational risk in multi-repo IaC estates; backend-block validation is a cheap, copyable control to look for in due diligence of engineering orgs.
insights.quote: Before down-scoping, RPP checks that the Terraform code path matches the specific S3 backend and KMS key for that workspace.
insights.locator: That role reads a source-of-truth configuration file

insights.claim: The genuinely novel piece of RPP is not OIDC role chaining or workspace-to-role mapping, which are standard, but the backend-block validation that guards against cross-workspace state corruption.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Separates signal from marketing when evaluating IaC security claims: role mapping is commodity, state-file binding is not.
insights.quote: However, the strong focus on backend-block validation is important. It acts as a guardrail against cross-workspace state corruption.
insights.locator: RPP is a private system, not open-source

insights.claim: RPP is a private, closed system that Pinterest has not open-sourced, so the transferable asset is the pattern (source-of-truth config, backend validation, down-scoped role assumption) rather than the code.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: No adoption flywheel or ecosystem to track here; the pattern will diffuse via write-ups and reimplementation, leaving room for a vendor to productise it.
insights.quote: RPP is a private system, not open-source.
insights.locator: RPP is a private system, not open-source

insights.claim: Pinterest's Terraform code is still scattered across many repositories each owned by a different team, with a mono-repo consolidation in progress but unfinished.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Even at a large well-resourced engineering org, IaC consolidation is a multi-year unfinished project — a realistic base rate for anyone modelling platform-migration timelines.
insights.quote: A consolidation into a mono-repo is still in progress.

insights.claim: Granting a CI/CD system broad permissions across many repositories and AWS accounts is framed as the core risk vector, raising the odds of both accidental misconfiguration and malicious action.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: The CI system is now the highest-value credential in a cloud estate; supply-chain and CI compromise is where cloud-security spend logically migrates next.
insights.quote: Granting a CI/CD system wide permissions to make changes across many repositories and AWS accounts can lead to a big risk.
insights.locator: Granting a CI/CD system wide permissions

insights.claim: The workspace-path-role mapping pattern lets teams enforce least privilege in PR-driven Terraform pipelines without first completing a full mono-repo migration, decoupling the security fix from the refactor.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Security controls that ship independently of large migrations get funded first; watch for tooling that sells this decoupling.
insights.quote: Teams can use it to enforce least privilege in PR-driven Terraform pipelines without needing a full mono-repo migration.
insights.locator: The workspace-path-role mapping pattern is a helpful guide

insights.claim: Centralising execution into shared composite actions means a systemic flaw such as a weak CI runner shell can be remediated in one place instead of across hundreds of separate repositories.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Blast-radius-of-fix is the quantifiable ROI argument for platform-engineering teams; it is the metric to press on when a platform investment is being justified.
insights.quote: a systemic issue, like a weak CI runner shell, can be fixed in one place instead of in hundreds of separate repositories
insights.locator: Pinterest says the model provides a single control point

insights.claim: The centralised pipeline embeds consistent PR-triggered checks including static analysis with custom Semgrep rules plus AI-assisted scanning, and optional LocalStack-based dry runs against mocked AWS behaviour before changes touch real accounts.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: AI-assisted code scanning is being adopted as a routine pipeline stage alongside deterministic SAST, not as a replacement — supportive for scanning vendors that layer AI on rules rather than pure-LLM entrants.
insights.quote: This includes static analysis with custom Semgrep rules and AI-assisted scanning.
insights.locator: The centralized composite actions help the team

insights.claim: Mercari's Terraform monorepo started from a single broad GCP service account holding owner rights across all projects, and was remediated with keyless Cloud Build credentials plus a read-only plan account and a per-service apply account using impersonation to confine each job to one project.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Same convergent design on both AWS and GCP: keyless CI identity plus split plan/apply identities is becoming the cross-cloud reference architecture.
insights.quote: It started with one broad GCP service account that had owner rights for all projects.

insights.claim: Slack took the opposite structural bet from Pinterest, decentralising Terraform state ownership to individual teams while still enforcing a plan-then-apply gate and mandatory promotion through sandbox and development before production.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: There is no settled winner between centralised and decentralised IaC state ownership; the invariant across both is the plan/apply gate, which is the control that actually matters.
insights.quote: Slack chose a different approach. They decentralized state ownership to individual teams.

insights.claim: The central design tension in centralised IaC is that the pipeline itself becomes a single point of failure, which layered controls (role mapping, backend validation, dual control) are meant to offset.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Concentration risk in the deploy plane is the next place incidents originate; a compromised central IaC pipeline would be a systemic, not local, event.
insights.quote: This helps keep centralized IaC pipelines safe from becoming a single point of failure.
